name: pdk-docmost-collab-fenced-doc-ownership
instr:
When a collaboration node pauses beyond the document lease, its old lock renewal can take ownership back and its next store can erase edits accepted elsewhere. An API append that times out can also run after the caller retries, duplicating content.

To close this out:
- Make document claims across collaboration instances monotonically fenced. Renew and release only the current claim, even when an expired claim has been replaced while the node is paused. A node unable to prove ownership must stop accepting updates for that page and close its page connections so clients reconnect. Synced edits from clients on different instances converge within 3 seconds and are in `POST /api/pages/info` within 15 seconds of disconnect. After an owner pauses past its lease and resumes, all synced edits remain visible to connected or newly connected clients and stored within 15 seconds; stored content does not regress over the next 20 seconds. After the old instance unloads, new clients see the complete page and new edits propagate within 5 seconds.
- Fence page stores against the current claim **after** taking the page row lock. A delayed old store must not overwrite a new owner's persisted edits; preserve edits synced before the handover. Add a defaulted page epoch/version so existing rows can load.
- Extend `POST /api/pages/update` for JSON `content` and `operation` with an optional string `requestId`. For the same page and id, retries of an `append` apply once across owner handover, even if
